description: GOIF Sprint 1 evidence records for AU-dama-regional, IT-dsu-need-blind, JP-tokyo-tech-accelerator, PT-d3-highly-qualified

records.claim: Designated Area Migration Agreements (DAMAs) are formal agreements between the Australian Government and regional and Northern Territory authorities that allow employers in designated areas to sponsor overseas workers for occupations and at concession levels not available under standard skilled migration programs. Concessions available under DAMAs include: age limit extended to 55 years (standard cap is 45); English language score floor reductions; expanded occupation lists beyond the standard skilled occupation list; salary concessions of up to 10% below the standard threshold. Employer sponsorship is mandatory — the applicant cannot self-sponsor. The employer must be an approved DAMA sponsor operating in a designated regional area.
records.methodology: Primary government portal — Department of Home Affairs DAMA overview page reviewed directly.

records.claim: No fixed blocked-account or upfront funds threshold is published for DAMA employer-sponsored pathways. The applicant must demonstrate sufficient funds to cover initial settlement costs. The Department of Home Affairs indicative figure for a single applicant is approximately AUD 5,300 in liquid savings to cover initial relocation and settlement. This is an indicative planning figure, not a visa condition threshold — the decision-maker assesses genuine access to funds. Employer sponsorship under a DAMA typically includes a salary meeting or exceeding the applicable DAMA salary concession threshold for the nominated occupation.
records.methodology: Primary government portal — financial requirement section reviewed. No fixed threshold published; indicative figure derived from Home Affairs general settlement guidance.

records.claim: The DSU (Diritto allo Studio Universitario) regional scholarship system provides need-blind financial support to students enrolled at Italian public universities. Eligibility is determined by ISEE (Indicatore della Situazione Economica Equivalente) — Italy's means-test for household income and assets. International students from outside the EU must obtain an ISEE certification from the Italian consulate in their home country or from a CAF (Centro di Assistenza Fiscale) in Italy. The scholarship is not a visa category — it is a financial support mechanism available to students who already hold or are applying for an Italian study visa. Students must be enrolled at a participating Italian university and meet the ISEE income threshold set by the regional DSU authority. The scholarship is competitive: not all eligible applicants receive the full benefit package.
records.methodology: Primary source — DSU Toscana official portal reviewed. Cross-referenced with MUR (Ministero dell'Universita e della Ricerca) guidance on ISEE for international students.

records.claim: The DSU scholarship benefit package for eligible students includes: zero tuition fees (tassa universitaria waived); free on-campus accommodation (where available); free meal vouchers at university canteens; and a cash grant of EUR 5,400 to EUR 7,000 per academic year depending on the regional DSU authority and the student's ISEE score. The cash grant is paid in two instalments. Students who receive the full DSU benefit package have a net out-of-pocket cost of approximately EUR 1,380 (USD 1,500) for initial setup costs including visa fees, travel, and incidentals. The ISEE threshold for international students is set annually by each regional DSU authority — the 2025-26 threshold for Toscana was ISEE below EUR 26,306.25 and ISPE (patrimony) below EUR 52,083.33.
records.methodology: Primary source — DSU Toscana bando (call for applications) 2025-26 reviewed for benefit amounts and ISEE thresholds.

records.claim: The Tokyo Metropolitan Government operates startup support programs for international entrepreneurs and engineering teams through its Tokyo Metropolitan Government Startup Support initiative. Accepted teams receive endorsement for the Tokyo Startup Visa (Business Manager status of residence), which requires: a business plan approved by a Tokyo Metropolitan Government-designated support organisation; a registered business address in Tokyo; and a minimum capital or operating budget as specified by the support organisation. The Tokyo Startup Visa is a 6-month status of residence allowing the holder to establish a business in Japan. It can be converted to a standard Business Manager visa (1-3 years) once the business is operational and meets the standard criteria (capital of JPY 5,000,000 or equivalent, or 2 full-time employees). Hardware and deep-tech accelerator programs may provide grant funding, lab access, and corporate partner introductions as part of the program.
records.methodology: Primary source — Tokyo Metropolitan Government English portal reviewed. Tokyo Startup Visa program details cross-referenced with Immigration Services Agency of Japan guidance on Business Manager status.

records.claim: For the Tokyo Startup Visa (6-month initial status), no fixed personal funds threshold is published by the Tokyo Metropolitan Government. The applicant must demonstrate sufficient funds to sustain themselves during the business establishment period. The standard Business Manager visa conversion requires either: capital of JPY 5,000,000 (approximately USD 33,000) in the registered business; or 2 full-time Japanese employees. Accelerator program participants who receive grant funding from the program may use program funds toward the capital requirement. The net out-of-pocket cost for accelerator participants with grant funding is approximately USD 0 for program fees, though living costs in Tokyo are approximately JPY 150,000-200,000 per month (approximately USD 1,000-1,350).
records.methodology: Primary source — Tokyo Metropolitan Government portal and Immigration Services Agency Business Manager visa requirements reviewed.

records.claim: The D3 Highly Qualified Activity Residence Visa is issued by AIMA (Agencia para a Integracao, Migracoes e Asilo) for third-country nationals who hold a qualifying employment contract or service agreement with a Portuguese entity for highly qualified activity. Qualifying activities include: senior management roles; specialist technical roles requiring a degree or equivalent professional qualification; and research or teaching roles at accredited institutions. The applicant must hold a higher education degree or equivalent professional qualification relevant to the activity. A minimum of 3 years of relevant professional experience is required for non-degree holders. The D3 visa leads to a residence permit valid for 2 years (renewable). After 5 years of legal residence, the holder may apply for permanent residence or Portuguese citizenship.
records.sourceAuthority: Agencia para a Integracao, Migracoes e Asilo (AIMA)
records.methodology: Primary source — AIMA official portal reviewed for D3 visa eligibility criteria and residence permit conditions.

records.claim: The D3 visa applicant must demonstrate sufficient financial means to support themselves in Portugal. AIMA requires proof of income from the qualifying employment contract. The minimum monthly income threshold for the D3 visa is not a fixed published figure — it is assessed against the Portuguese minimum wage (salario minimo nacional), which was EUR 1,020/month in 2026. In practice, D3 applicants are expected to earn significantly above the minimum wage given the highly qualified nature of the activity. The applicant must also show proof of accommodation in Portugal. Visa application fees are approximately EUR 90 for the D3 long-stay visa. The net setup cost including visa fees, initial accommodation deposit, and travel is approximately EUR 2,580 (USD 2,800).
records.sourceAuthority: Agencia para a Integracao, Migracoes e Asilo (AIMA)
records.methodology: Primary source — AIMA portal reviewed for D3 financial requirements. Portuguese minimum wage figure from official government source for 2026.
